info.title: FetchX engine private API
info.description: The contract between the FetchX platform and the FetchX engine. Private network only; every call carries the platform's service token. The engine never sees prices, credits or users: jobs carry an opaque tenant, the platform sends the cost tiers a job may use (allowed_steps) and bills from `usage`, which only a successful job has. Finished jobs are also reported as signed job.finished events (see JobFinishedEvent). POST /internal/v1/estimates says what requests would take before they are sent (planned tiers, per-host history and pace), for the platform to price. Batches are the platform's: it checks a batch's requests with POST /internal/v1/requests/check, asks POST /internal/v1/pace how fast each host may take work, and starts each item as a paced job (JobInput.paced), which the engine refuses with host_busy when the host has no free slot. info.version is the contract version; GET /internal/v1/status and /healthz report it. Saved site logins (1.13): a tenant saves a site's username and password with POST /internal/v1/logins (sealed, never returned); a job whose page asks for a sign-in on that site signs in with it in the browser, keeps the signed-in session for the tenant's later jobs, and reports how it went (Attempt.sign_in, errors login_required and login_failed). Browser actions and host allowlists (1.14): a job's actions run in order in its browser once the page has loaded, each with its result in FetchData.actions (error action_failed, free); allow_hosts limits every request and connection to the listed hosts (FetchData.blocked_requests); over HTTP, redirect manual returns a redirect itself and all_headers returns the headers as sent (FetchData.redirects, location, raw_headers). Remote browser sessions (1.16): POST /internal/v1/browser-sessions starts a Camoufox the caller drives itself over Playwright's protocol, held to allow_hosts like a job's browser (every request a page, frame or worker makes is admitted by the engine; WebSockets and other connections go through the engine's relay, which opens tunnels only to hosts on the list). The caller connects with Playwright's connect() through the platform, which carries the WebSocket upgrade to GET /internal/v1/browser-sessions/{id}/ws?tenant=<tenant> with the service token (not a routed path: the server takes the upgrade). A session ends when the platform closes it (DELETE), at its TTL, when its caller is idle or gone for idle_ttl_s, at max_wire_bytes, or when its browser fails; its receipt (BrowserSession, state closed) says why, what it used and whether it is billable. The engine never records protocol payloads, page input or screenshots of a session.

400.description: The envelope or the request is wrong; nothing was started. Codes: invalid_request, url_not_allowed, secret_not_allowed_here (secrets with an option that keeps or sends what a page shows elsewhere, or a paced batch item; details.field names it).

402.description: No planned step is in allowed_steps; nothing was started. Codes: budget_too_low.

post.summary: Start a job for the page after job {id}'s, or return the existing one for its idempotency key
post.description: Job {id} must be the tenant's, finished and successful, with data.next_page and its content not yet deleted. A next link is fetched like any URL; a next page reached by clicking or scrolling loads the list again on the same residential session and repeats the steps back to the earlier page first. The new job is billed like any other: usage only on success.

202.description: Still running; poll GET /internal/v1/jobs/{id} with the new id.

409.description: Refused. Codes: idempotency_conflict, job_id_conflict, pending (job {id} is still running), no_next_page (details.reason: failed, none_found, limit or url_not_allowed).

410.description: Job {id} has nothing to go on from. Codes: content_expired (its content has expired or was deleted, so its cookies are gone), not_stored (a job made with store: false keeps no session for a next page).

post.summary: What requests would take, before they are sent
post.description: Plans each request as POST /internal/v1/jobs would (with every tier allowed) and reports, per request, the cost tiers its ladder would try in order and the one site knowledge has proven; per host, what its recent requests took (site usage: the winning tier, wire bytes, captcha solves and seconds, over the last 100 requests within 30 days) and how fast a batch may start requests to it. Nothing is sent to any site and no tenant's data is read. A request that would be refused is reported in its item, and the others are still estimated.

post.summary: Start a remote browser session; answers once its caller can connect
post.description: Takes a browser worker for the session's whole life and answers when the session's browser is up (state open, expires_at set), usually within seconds and at most about a minute. The caller then connects with Playwright's connect(), with the exact Playwright version in playwright.version (another version is refused with HTTP 428 at the WebSocket), and drives browser.contexts[0], the session's one context. The same id again answers with the session as it stands (201) and starts nothing.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: The platform project id.

post.summary: Type one of the session's secrets into a field, without the caller ever holding it
post.description: Types the named secret (one of the session's own, or login.username / login.password of its saved login) into the first element matching selector, in the newest page's frame whose URL starts with frame_url (the main frame when left out). The frame must be on https, on a host the session has reached, at one of the secret's origins (a login's: its site). From then on the value is taken out of everything the session sends its caller (as [REDACTED:<name>], or [REDACTED] for a login's), and a request carrying it to another origin is stopped (secret_egress in the receipt).

403.description: Codes: secret_origin_mismatch (the frame is not at one of the secret's origins), secret_insecure (not https).

404.description: Codes: not_found (no such session), secret_not_found (no secret by that name).

409.description: Codes: fill_frame_not_found, fill_failed (details.reason: no element matched, or it took no input).

ServiceToken.description: The platform's service token; the engine stores only its SHA-256 (config.platform.tokenHashes, two during a rotation).

rendered.description: True when a browser produced the result.

content_expired.description: True after 7 days or DELETE: everything below is gone.

cookies.description: Cookies the site set, for multi-step flows: those for the final URL, then those a redirect hop set for another host or path. On an HTTP step each cookie a hop wrote says which (hop, 0 for the first response); the last write per name, domain and path wins, and a cookie a hop expired is left out.

redirects.description: HTTP steps only: the redirects followed, in order, each with the URL that answered, its status, where it pointed and the names of the cookies it set. Empty when the first response was the answer.

location.description: With redirect: manual, when the answer is a redirect: its Location, resolved against the request URL (null when it is not a URL).

raw_headers.description: With all_headers: the response's headers as [name, value] pairs, in the order sent, with duplicates (each Set-Cookie). An HTTP step keeps the site's casing; a browser step reports what the browser gives, lowercased. At most 200 pairs, values cut at 8 KB.

actions.description: With actions: one entry per action, in order (null when the step that answered never got to them).

blocked_requests.description: With allow_hosts: what was refused for being off the list, at most 100, each origin and type once per action.

passive_offlist_hosts.description: With allow_passive_subresources, on a browser step: the origins off the list the page loaded scripts, styles, fonts or images from.

body.description: The body: utf-8 text, or base64 for binary. Only when formats has body (the default); left out on reads with include_body=false, and when it is too large to inline (see body_url).

body_url.description: Where to download a body too large to inline.

skeleton.description: With formats: skeleton, the shape of a JSON body; null when the body is not JSON.

extract.description: The JSON read from the page for the request's extract: an object for a one-record schema (fields the page does not show are null), an array of records for a list schema. null when the site answered 404 or 410. Only on requests with extract.

screenshot.description: formats: screenshot, base64 JPEG. Also at /v1/fetch/{id}/screenshot.

page.description: Where this page sits in a list read page by page. On successful results.

number.description: 1 for a first fetch; each next page adds 1.

previous_id.description: The job this one is the next page of.

screens.description: Screens scrolled reading this page (for a next page that loads on scroll, past where the earlier page ended). 0 when it was not scrolled.

end.description: true: scrolling reached the end of the page and nothing more loaded; false: scrolling stopped (screens or time) while there was more; null: not scrolled.

next_page.description: On successful HTML results: how the page leads on, or null when FetchX found no next page. Open it with POST .../jobs/{id}/next.

hop.description: HTTP steps: the response that set it, 0 for the first (see redirects). Left out for a cookie the attempt already had.

rotation.description: A fresh residential IP for the same step.

result.description: not_admitted means nothing reached the site on this step (for example the provider refused the host); it does not count as an attempt. content_missing means the page loaded without what expect asked for, or without a required extract field.

code.description: The underlying error, when result is not_admitted or failed.

challenge.description: On a blocked or rate-limited step, the bot-protection vendor whose wall it was, when known (for example datadome, cloudflare, akamai, imperva, human, aws_waf, kasada; or arkose, recaptcha, hcaptcha, mtcaptcha when only its captcha says).

missing.description: On a content_missing step, the expect conditions the page did not meet, and extract:<field> for each required extract field it did not show.

wire_bytes.description: Bytes this step moved over the network, requests and responses together. On a residential route this is the traffic billed past the included megabytes.

captcha.description: Captchas met on this step, as type:outcome. passed: the page let the visitor through; still_challenged: the same captcha came back; still_blocked: the captcha went away but the site kept refusing; other outcomes say why no solve was made (for example captcha_timeout). Only a request that succeeds is charged for its captchas.

warmup.description: Browser steps on sites that have refused FetchX before start at the site's home page (a data step on such a host starts at the call's page, see from_page). passed: it loaded; cleared: a bot check there cleared by itself; solved: the check there was a captcha, which was solved, and the visit went on (see captcha); challenged: the check stayed, so this step ended there and the next one used a fresh IP; failed: the home page did not load, and the page was visited directly.

wall.description: A bot check on the page itself: whether it cleared by itself before any captcha was solved.

client_profile.description: The client the site saw: FetchX's own HTTP client (node), Chrome's TLS and HTTP/2 on a handoff (chrome136), the Camoufox browser (camoufox), or the CloakBrowser browser (cloakbrowser: a Chromium presenting a Windows device, tried on a fresh exit after Camoufox met a wall, and first on a host where it gets through more often).

handoff.description: An HTTP step on a residential session a browser got through for this project and host earlier (the handoff): same exit IP, the cookies that browser earned and its User-Agent, sent with Chrome's TLS. Only for requests that need no browser and bring no cookie or Authorization of their own: data (not GET or HEAD, or an Accept that is not HTML) or render: never.

from_page.description: A browser step for data (a GET or HEAD whose Accept is not HTML) on a host that refuses FetchX, whose call was made from the page it belongs to: the browser opened the caller's Referer (else its Origin, else the site's home page) on the same site, let it settle, and the page made the call with fetch() and the caller's headers, adding the telemetry its bot protection hands the page's own calls (Akamai Bot Manager's Akamai-BM-Telemetry). A call to another origin is made this way only with such telemetry; otherwise the browser goes on from the page to the URL itself. The call's answer is the step's answer. A session whose call carried telemetry gets no handoff (a value works only from the browser it was made for): the project's later data requests on it are made from its page again, in the browser kept open for it when there is one.

ips_skipped.description: A residential browser step: fresh draws passed over before the browser opened, because the host had walled their exit IP in the last day or keeps walling their exit network.

warm.description: A residential browser step's warm session: kept, the browser that got the session through stays open for the session's next page in this project; reused, the page was read in that open browser (same cookies and exit IP), with no warm-up.

content.description: Browser steps on pages that answered: settled when the page had stopped filling itself in (results, listings loaded by script) before it was read; still_loading when the engine's wait ran out first, so the page may be missing content that loads late. wait_for with a selector waits longer for what is needed.

content_ms.description: Browser steps on pages that answered: how long the engine waited for the page to fill itself in, scrolling included.

screens.description: Browser steps on pages that answered: the screens scrolled after the page filled in, to load what appears as a reader scrolls. 0 when it was not scrolled: the page fit on one screen, or the wait used up its time first.

scroll.description: How the page was scrolled, when screens is above 0: by mouse wheel, or by script when a wheel did not move the page (a sheet that locks the page takes the wheel).

requests.description: Browser steps that answered: the requests the page made that FetchX let through (the page, its scripts, images and data).

refused.description: Browser steps that answered: the page's requests that FetchX did not let through, by reason (for example url_not_allowed, insecure_request, request_limit, source_dns_failed). Absent when there were none.

sign_in.description: A sign-in on the page with the saved login: passed (signed in), rejected (the sign-in form came back), code_required (it asked for a one-time code), failed (no clear answer), no_login (the page asked for a sign-in on a host no usable saved login covers).

secrets_used.description: true on the attempt that typed or sent one of the request's secrets (no attempt follows it).

reason.description: For example excluded_by_provider_rule, over_max_credits, cooling or handoff_unavailable (the handoff's session was taken by a browser meanwhile).

action_index.description: action_failed: the action that failed (data.actions[i].error says why).

next.description: What to do next. A request key replays its first result, failures included, so a retry always needs a new idempotency_key.

retry_after_seconds.description: The earliest time a retry can help.

retry_with_new_key.description: true: the same request may succeed if sent again with a new idempotency_key (after retry_after_seconds when given). false: sent again unchanged it would fail the same way; change it as action says.

url.description: The page, API or file to get. Public http or https only: private, local and metadata addresses are refused, checked after DNS and on every redirect. A #fragment is never sent to the site, but a browser opens the page with it, and an app route in it (#/... or #!/...) makes auto start in a browser, since plain HTTP gets the same empty app for every route.

method.description: Only GET and HEAD escalate. Other methods get one attempt, never a browser, and are never retried.

headers.description: Headers for the site, cookies and Authorization included (stored encrypted, never logged). Up to 64 headers and 16 KB. Host, hop-by-hop, Forwarded and X-Forwarded-* are refused.

body.description: A text request body, up to 1 MB. Only with POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.

body_base64.description: A binary request body in base64, instead of body.

render.description: auto tries HTTP first and moves to a browser when HTTP is blocked or the page is an empty JavaScript shell; always starts in a browser; never stays on HTTP.

wait_for.description: In a browser, wait for a CSS selector or a fixed time. Implies a browser.

scroll.description: How far a page opened in a browser is scrolled. auto (the default): once it has filled in, scroll while scrolling loads more, up to 10 screens. off: read it once it has filled in, without scrolling. A number from 1 to 50: scroll up to that many screens, stopping early at the end of the page; implies a browser. Scrolling is not charged, but what it loads is traffic like any other.

country.description: The exit country for proxy routes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Defaults to the country that worked for this site before, else US. When it is left to FetchX and a site keeps walling one country's exit IPs (two walls in a row on residential browsers), the next fresh IPs come from another country; each attempt reports the country it used. Set it to stay in one country.

route.description: One fixed route; turns auto mode off: one attempt, with a precise error.

country.description: Required for datacenter and residential; null for direct.

render.description: true uses a browser on this route.

formats.description: What to return. body: the response as received (the rendered page after a browser), the default when formats is left out. markdown, text, links and metadata are derived from it; skeleton: the shape of a JSON body (keys, types, array lengths and a small sample), a few KB instead of the whole body, null when the body is not JSON; screenshot needs a browser. Ask only for what you use: a rendered page can be megabytes of HTML. The body is stored either way and can be downloaded from /v1/fetch/{id}/content.

block_resources.description: In a browser, do not download images, video, audio or web fonts on the page. They carry none of the text but a good part of a rendered page’s traffic, and residential traffic past the included megabytes is charged per MB; the text and every image URL stay in the page. Captcha widgets still load theirs. On a site whose bot protection has walled FetchX, and on any attempt after a wall, the browser loads everything anyway, since a bot check can notice an image or font that never loads. Defaults to true, or false when formats has screenshot.

expect.description: What the page must show to be the content you want. Every condition given must hold, or the step is not a success: auto mode tries a browser, then one fresh IP, and a request that never gets it fails with content_missing and is not charged. A browser waits up to 10 s for the selector after the page settles. A real 404 or 410 is the site’s answer and is not checked.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match at least one element (HTML only).

text.description: Text that must appear in the page’s visible text (or a non-HTML body), ignoring case and spacing.

min_markdown_length.description: The page’s markdown (a non-HTML body’s text) must have at least this many characters.

extract.description: Read the page into JSON. schema is a small JSON Schema whose descriptions say what each field is: a root object asks for one record (a product, an article), a root array of objects (with a description of one record) asks for every record of that kind on a list page. Fields: string (format date, date-time or uri), number, integer, boolean, enum of strings, and arrays of strings or numbers; up to 30 per record. Every value is checked against the page: one the page does not show is null, never guessed. A field listed in required that the page does not show makes the step content_missing, as a missed expect does (the ladder tries a browser, then a fresh IP; never billed). The page is fetched only when extraction can run (else 503 extract_unavailable); if the models fail after the page is fetched, the job fails with extract_unavailable and is not billed. The result is data.extract with data.extract_report; usage.extract says how much page text was read. Not with HEAD.

schema.description: type object (one record) or array (items: an object, description required, maxItems up to 200). additionalProperties may only be false. At most 16 KB.

instructions.description: Optional context for every field, for example which of several prices to take.

max_attempts.description: The most attempts that may reach the site. Steps refused before anything is sent do not count.

fix_headers.description: Replace automation User-Agents (curl, python-requests…) with a browser one and add a missing Accept and Accept-Language.

max_credits.description: Passed through from the customer. The platform enforces the ceiling and turns it into allowed_steps; the engine keeps it only in the idempotency hash.

timeout_ms.description: Total time for all attempts. A captcha solve can take up to a minute, so the default leaves room for one; a synchronous call still answers 202 after 60 seconds if the request is not finished. Up to 180000, or 300000 with actions.

async.description: true answers 202 at once; false waits up to 60 seconds, then answers 202.

webhook_url.description: A public https URL that receives the result when the request finishes.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same result and is charged once. Generated when absent.

tags.description: Your labels, to filter the list.

capture.description: Record the page's own network calls (its documents, XHR and fetch requests) while a browser renders it, and keep them with the result for as long as its other content (7 days). Read them with GET /internal/v1/jobs/{id}/network, /internal/v1/jobs/{id}/network/{index} and /internal/v1/jobs/{id}/network.har. true records with the defaults; false or null records nothing. capture needs a browser, so with render: auto it makes the request render, and it is refused (invalid_request, details.field capture) with render: never, a method other than GET, or a route whose render is false. Free: it adds nothing to the price. When several browsers are tried, the calls are the last browser attempt's, also when the request fails.

redirect.description: follow: follow redirects (up to 5, each hop checked). manual: answer with the redirect itself: data.status_code is the 3xx, data.final_url the request URL and data.location where it points. Manual is HTTP only: auto mode uses no browser, and render always, route.render, wait_for, screenshot, a number of screens and capture are refused (invalid_request, field redirect). Cookies the 3xx sets come back in data.cookies.

all_headers.description: Return the response's headers as sent in data.raw_headers: in order, with duplicates (each Set-Cookie) and, on HTTP steps, the site's casing.

actions.description: Steps for a browser to take, in order, once the page has loaded (its load event, at most 10 s): wait, click, fill, press, select, scroll, navigate, evaluate a script, wait for a response and more. They run in one tab, in one page and one JavaScript realm: what an evaluate leaves on window stays for later actions until the page navigates. Selectors are Playwright CSS and reach into open shadow roots. Actions imply a browser: method must be GET, render must not be never, redirect must not be manual, a route's render defaults to true (false is refused), and a number of screens to scroll is refused (use a scroll action). Only the browser steps of auto mode are used, and a route runs one attempt. The page is not scrolled or read further after the last action: data.body is its DOM then, data.final_url its address and data.status_code the last top-level document's status. expect and extract read that page. A popup or new tab is closed. Billed as one browser step, with nothing per action; a request whose action failed is free. At most 512 KB as JSON in all.

action_timeout_ms.description: Only with actions: the timeout_ms of every action that does not give its own.

allow_hosts.description: The only hosts the request may reach: exact hostnames, or *.suffix for every subdomain of suffix (not suffix itself). The URL's host must be on the list (else 400 url_not_allowed, field url). In a browser it covers every request and connection the page makes (navigations, frames, scripts, XHR and fetch, WebSockets, workers, redirect hops): one to a host off the list is refused before it leaves FetchX and listed in data.blocked_requests by origin. Over HTTP a redirect to a host off the list is not followed: the 3xx is the answer, with data.location. Captcha widgets load from their vendors' hosts, which are off most lists. A navigate action to a host off the list is refused (400, field actions[i].url).

allow_passive_subresources.description: Only with allow_hosts: let the page load scripts, styles, fonts and images from hosts off the list (GET only, sent without Cookie or Authorization), listed in data.passive_offlist_hosts. Documents, frames, XHR and fetch, WebSockets, beacons, form posts and workers stay on the list.

login.description: A saved site login (POST /internal/v1/logins). Left out: the tenant's login whose site shares the request's registrable domain, if it has exactly one, signs in when a page asks for a sign-in on a host it covers, and its saved session goes with the request. An id names the login to use (for a sign-in on another domain); false never signs in. Ignored when the request sends its own Cookie or Authorization header. Once a sign-in sent the login, the request makes no further attempts.

value.description: At most 4096 bytes. Never stored, logged or returned: held in the engine's memory while the request runs, and taken out of everything the request returns (as [REDACTED:<name>]) in the forms a page may send or show it (as typed, URL-encoded, form-encoded, JSON-escaped, base64). Shorter than 4 characters is refused: it could not be found to redact.

origins.description: The https origins (scheme, host, port; no path) the secret may be typed into or sent to. Each host must be in allow_hosts.

secrets.description: The request's own secrets by name (1 to 8), each typed or sent only to the origins it names. A fill_secret action types one into a field when the field's frame is at one of its origins (else the action fails with secret_origin_mismatch); {{secret.<name>}} in body or a header value is filled in over HTTP (form-encoded in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, JSON-escaped in a JSON one), on each hop whose origin the secret names (a hop that would carry it elsewhere is not sent: secret_egress_blocked); the URL's origin must be one of them, and a GET or HEAD with placeholders needs render never. While a secret is loaded in a browser, a request the page makes that carries it (URL, headers or body) to another origin is stopped, and the request fails with secret_egress_blocked. Once a secret was typed or sent, the request makes no further attempt (on any route). Requires allow_hosts. Refused (400 secret_not_allowed_here, details.field) with formats screenshot, extract, capture.unmask, webhook_url, and in batches. Forces store false. The request keeps each secret's name and origins only, and its hash is keyed.

store.description: false: nothing the site sent outlives its first read, and nothing the caller sent to the site is kept. The first GET of the finished job with its body (the synchronous answer, or a poll) gives the content in full (the body always inline) and deletes it; it is deleted at the latest 15 minutes after the job finished. After that the job keeps only its summary (status, page_status, error, attempts, secrets_used) with data null, for 90 days, and its content routes and next page answer 410 not_stored. The kept request has no headers, body or action values. Forced false with secrets.

FetchRequest.description: The customer request exactly as the platform received it on POST /v1/fetch.

page_status.description: What the page was. content: the page you asked for (with expect, it showed what you expected). not_found: the site’s real 404 or 410, billed like content. empty: it loaded but showed next to nothing, or not what expect asked for. challenge: a bot wall, block or rate limit stopped it (see challenge). login_required: the site asked for a sign-in, and FetchX had no saved login for it or the site did not accept the one it had (error login_required or login_failed). error: anything else (see error). Null while pending.

data.description: What the site answered: on success the real answer, on failure the last response. Null only when nothing reached the site.

challenge.description: The walls the request met on its way, or null when it met none.

attempts.description: One entry per step tried, in order. Providers are never named.

skipped.description: Steps that were not tried, and why.

network.description: Only on requests made with capture: the network capture (null while pending). Top level, not under data, because a request that failed before any page answered still has its capture.

secrets_used.description: Only on a request made with secrets: the names of those that were typed (fill_secret) or sent (a placeholder), sorted by name. Values never appear anywhere.

Job.description: The caller-facing view of a job. The platform adds `credits` and returns it as the public FetchResult.

Challenge.description: Blocks, bot challenges and rate limits met on the way, and on the page that answered (a captcha, a wall that cleared). FetchX handles them itself; this says what it met and how it got past.

vendor.description: The bot-protection vendor last seen (datadome, cloudflare, akamai, imperva, human, aws_waf, kasada, or the captcha provider when nothing else names one: arkose, recaptcha, hcaptcha, mtcaptcha), named from the wall page, its headers and cookies, also when the wall came as a rate limit (429); null when nothing said.

passed.description: Whether FetchX got past them to the page.

passed_by.description: rotation: a later attempt on another route or a fresh IP got through; captcha: solved on the page (10 credits); wait: it cleared by itself. Null when not passed.

Usage.description: What a successful job used; the platform prices it. Null for a failed or pending job, which is never billed.

extract.description: When the request had extract: the page text the models read (the platform prices it) and the model calls made.

id.description: Made by the platform; the job id customers see.

tenant.description: The platform project id. Every read must name it again.

allowed_steps.description: The cost tiers the reservation covers. Steps outside them are skipped (over_max_credits). Omitted or null allows every tier. Empty refuses with budget_too_low unless the idempotency key already has a job.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the result before answering 202. Defaults to the engine's sync wait (60 s). Ignored for async requests.

paced.description: A batch item: start only when the job's host has a free slot at its pace (see POST /internal/v1/pace), else refuse with 429 host_busy and start nothing. Every job, paced or not, holds a slot on its host while it runs.

webhook_url.description: The customer webhook; the platform delivers it after settling.

deadline.description: When the job stops trying. A pending job is finished (or recovered as uncertain) by then.

created.description: On POST only: false when the idempotency key already had a job (nothing new was started).

secrets_used.description: Only on a request made with secrets: the names of those that were typed or sent.

JobFinishedEvent.description: Sent to the platform (config.platform.eventsUrl) once per finished job, until it answers 2xx. Headers: x-fetchx-timestamp (Unix seconds) and x-fetchx-signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(eventKey, "<timestamp>.<raw body>").

AdminObject.description: An admin answer, passed through to the admin portal unchanged.

NextPageRequest.description: What may change for a next page; everything else (headers, formats, country, render, wait_for, block_resources) comes from the earlier request, and the cookies the site set on the earlier page are sent with it (with a saved login, its session's cookies instead).

scroll.description: As in FetchRequest; defaults to the earlier request's. For a next page that loads as the page is scrolled, it is how many more screens to scroll past where the earlier page ended (auto: up to 10 more); off is refused there.

expect.description: As in FetchRequest. Left out, the earlier request's expect applies; null drops it, for a list whose later pages do not show what the first one did.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match at least one element (HTML only).

text.description: Text that must appear in the page’s visible text (or a non-HTML body), ignoring case and spacing.

min_markdown_length.description: The page’s markdown (a non-HTML body’s text) must have at least this many characters.

max_credits.description: Passed through from the customer. The platform enforces the ceiling and turns it into allowed_steps; the engine keeps it only in the idempotency hash.

timeout_ms.description: Total time for all attempts. A captcha solve can take up to a minute, so the default leaves room for one; a synchronous call still answers 202 after 60 seconds if the request is not finished.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same result and is charged once. Generated when absent.

capture.description: As in the fetch request. Left out, the earlier request's capture applies; false or null turns it off. The calls carry this page's number in `page`, so a client can compare page 1's and page 2's calls.

id.description: Made by the platform; the new job's id.

tenant.description: The platform project id. Every read must name it again.

allowed_steps.description: The cost tiers the reservation covers. Steps outside them are skipped (over_max_credits). Omitted or null allows every tier. Empty refuses with budget_too_low unless the idempotency key already has a job.

wait_ms.description: How long to wait for the result before answering 202. Defaults to the engine's sync wait (60 s). Ignored for async requests.

paced.description: A batch item: start only when the job's host has a free slot at its pace (see POST /internal/v1/pace), else refuse with 429 host_busy and start nothing. Every job, paced or not, holds a slot on its host while it runs.

how.description: link: a link to the next page (url); click: a next or load-more control the page handles itself; scroll: the list loads more as it is scrolled further.

url.description: For link: the next page's address.

requests.description: Requests as POST /internal/v1/jobs takes them in `request`. One that is not valid is reported in its item.

Spread.description: The median (p50) and 90th percentile (p90) of the samples; null when there are none.

share.description: This tier's share of the successful requests (0 to 1).

captcha_share.description: Share of this tier's successes that solved a captcha (0 to 1).

SiteUsage.description: What a host's recent requests took: the last 100 finished requests within 30 days, from every tenant (host name only). Failures count only when they say something about the site (blocked, rate_limited, unreachable, site_error, timeout); pages read past the default depth are left out.

steps.description: Per tier that got the data.

since.description: When the oldest of these requests finished.

Pace.description: How fast a batch starts requests to this host: open (never refused FetchX), guarded (refused or rate-limited it before), limited (rate-limited it in the last ten minutes).

steps.description: The tiers the request may dispatch, in order, up to max_attempts (an explicit route is one step). Rotations used only after a rate limit are left out.

proven.description: The first step's tier when site knowledge has proven that route for the host.

cooling.description: Set when every route is resting and none has worked for this host: sent now, the request would fail with cooling_down.

error.description: Why POST /internal/v1/jobs would refuse this request (invalid_request, url_not_allowed, request_too_large).

defaults.description: Per tier across recently active hosts, for hosts with no history of their own.

ExtractReport.description: How the page was read for extract. On a failed request, why its page did not give the JSON.

status.description: complete: every required field was found. missing_required: a required field was not on the page (the step was content_missing). unavailable: the models could not run. skipped: the site answered 404 or 410, so nothing was read.

reason.description: For unavailable or skipped: not_configured, budget_exhausted, calls_exhausted, error or not_found.

page_tokens.description: Page text the models read, in tokens of 4 characters.

truncated.description: True when the page was longer than extraction reads (150,000 tokens), or the call cap or deadline stopped it; fields not reached are null.

records.description: Records returned for a list schema; null for one record.

dropped.description: List blocks left out: empty, repeated, or missing a required field.

source.description: List schema: records read one by one from the page's repeated blocks, or the whole list read at once.

fill.description: List schema: the share of records with each field found.

missing.description: One record: the fields that are null.

reasons.description: Why each missing field is null: not_found (the page does not show it), unsure (the models disagreed or were not confident), ungrounded (a value was read that is not on the page).

evidence.description: The page text the value was read from.

fields.description: One record: for each value found, how sure the model was and where on the page it was.

required_missing.description: The required fields the page did not show.

items.description: A FetchRequest as the caller sent it, valid or not: each result says whether the engine would take it.

host.description: The host the request is paced under (lowercase).

tier.description: open: the host never refused FetchX. guarded: it refused or rate-limited FetchX before. limited: one of its routes was rate-limited recently.

next_start_in_ms.description: 0: a paced job may start now. null: the host is full until a job finishes.

hosts.description: Keyed by the host as it is paced (lowercase), which is what POST /internal/v1/requests/check returns.

CaptureSettings.description: What to record. Every field is optional.

types.description: Which calls to record. Images, media, fonts, stylesheets, manifests and beacons are never recorded.

max_requests.description: Calls past this are counted in network.dropped.over_limit, not stored, and network.truncated is true.

max_body_bytes.description: Per response body. A longer body is cut and marked body_truncated. At most 25 MB of bodies are stored per request; later calls keep their headers and sizes, with body_omitted capture_full.

bodies.description: text: store bodies that are JSON, HTML, XML, plain text, JavaScript, GraphQL or form data. none: headers and sizes only. all: binary bodies too, as base64.

first_party_only.description: Keep only calls to the page's own registrable domain (example.com and *.example.com). Others are counted in network.dropped.third_party.

include_trackers.description: Keep calls to known analytics, advertising, tag manager and consent hosts, flagged tracker. By default they are dropped and counted in network.dropped.trackers.

unmask.description: Store and return secret header values in full instead of masked (see the headers of a call).

NetworkSummary.description: A request made with capture: how many calls were recorded and where to read them.

dropped.description: Calls seen and not stored, by reason.

truncated.description: max_requests was reached: later calls were counted, not stored.

attempt.description: The attempt (1 is the first entry of attempts) whose browser recorded these calls; null when no browser ran.

complete.description: false when the browser stopped (a deadline, a crash) before it reported everything: the calls it sent before are kept.

expires_at.description: When the calls are deleted with the rest of the content.

expired.description: true after DELETE: the calls are gone.

index.description: The call number, from 1 in the order the page made the calls.

page.description: 1 for the first page, 2 for the first POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next, and so on.

phase.description: warmup: FetchX's own visit to the site's home page before the page (protected sites); load: the page loading; scroll: after scrolling started; replay: FetchX getting back to the earlier page on a next page; sign_in: FetchX signing in with a saved login (the password is redacted); actions: while the caller's actions ran.

status.description: Null when no response came (see error).

response_bytes.description: Bytes received for the body, as transferred.

first_party.description: Whether the call went to the page's own registrable domain.

frame.description: Made by the page itself or by a frame inside it.

started_ms.description: When the call started, in ms from the start of the page's load (warm-up calls are negative).

body_omitted.description: Why a response body was not stored: not_text (capture.bodies text), bodies_none, capture_full (25 MB per request reached) or unavailable (the browser no longer had it).

error.description: Why a call got no response: refused:<reason> when FetchX refused it (refused:resource_blocked, refused:request_limit), a browser error such as browser_err_aborted, or not_finished when it was still open at the end.

matched.description: With contains: the values this call's response body holds.

action_index.description: The caller's action that set the call off (see ActionResponse.action_index_started), or null.

complete.description: Whether the call finished: false when it failed or was still open when the page was read.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page of calls.

index.description: The call number, from 1 in the order the page made the calls.

page.description: 1 for the first page, 2 for the first POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next, and so on.

phase.description: warmup: FetchX's own visit to the site's home page before the page (protected sites); load: the page loading; scroll: after scrolling started; replay: FetchX getting back to the earlier page on a next page; sign_in: FetchX signing in with a saved login (the password is redacted).

frame.description: Made by the page itself or by a frame inside it.

first_party.description: Whether the call went to the page's own registrable domain.

started_ms.description: When the call started, in ms from the start of the page's load (warm-up calls are negative).

error.description: Why a call got no response: refused:<reason> when FetchX refused it (refused:resource_blocked, refused:request_limit), a browser error such as browser_err_aborted, or not_finished when it was still open at the end.

headers.description: Name and value pairs in the order sent, so repeated headers survive. Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and any header whose name contains token, secret, api-key, session, password or credential show `<masked len=N sha=XXXXXX>` instead of the value (a cookie keeps its name), unless the request was made with capture.unmask.

Name and value pairs in the order sent, so repeated headers survive. Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and any header whose name contains token, secret, api-key, session, password or credential show `<masked len=N sha=XXXXXX>` instead of the value (a cookie keeps its name), unless the request was made with capture.unmask.

body.description: Decompressed. Text bodies as UTF-8; binary ones (capture.bodies all) as base64. Null when not stored, or over 1 MB (see body_url).

body_omitted.description: Why a response body was not stored: not_text (capture.bodies text), bodies_none, capture_full (25 MB per request reached) or unavailable (the browser no longer had it).

body_url.description: For a body over 1 MB: /internal/v1/jobs/{id}/network/{index}/body, read with the same key.

response.description: Null when no response came (see error).

redirected_from.description: The index of the call this one is a redirect of.

action_index.description: The caller's action that set the call off (see ActionResponse.action_index_started), or null.

complete.description: Whether the call finished: false when it failed or was still open when the page was read.

JsonSkeleton.description: The shape of a JSON body (formats: skeleton), a few KB however large the body. Fields are read from the first 100 elements of each array. A JSON document a browser shows inside a lone <pre> is read from there.

root.description: The type of the whole document.

fields.description: Each path once, in the order first seen.

path.description: JSONPath: $ for the document, $.items for a key, $.items[*].price for a key of each element, $['a.b'] for a key that needs quoting.

type.description: object, array, string, number, boolean or null; several joined with | when it varies (string|null).

seen.description: How many times the path was seen: compare with the parent array's items to spot optional keys.

items.description: For an array: elements across every time it was seen.

sample.description: The body with every array cut to its first element and long strings cut short (null when even that is too large).

truncated.description: Fields past 150, or deeper or longer than the limits, were left out, or the sample was cut further to fit.

ActionFrame.description: The frame to act in (default: the top frame): the first whose URL contains url_contains, or the iframe element selector matches. Waited for within the action's timeout; none gives frame_not_found.

Action.description: One step. Each type takes only its own fields (anything else is refused, invalid_request with details.field actions[i].name). Every action takes frame (not navigate, wait_for_url or wait_for_response), optional (a failed optional action does not stop the others) and timeout_ms (1 to 60000; an evaluate up to the request's timeout_ms). wait: ms (0 to 60000), or selector with state (attached, visible (default), hidden, detached). wait_for_url: url_contains or url_regex, matched against the top frame's URL. click: selector, button (left, right, middle), click_count (1 to 3); scrolls the element into view and waits until it can be clicked. hover: selector. fill: selector (default: the element with the focus, through open shadow roots) and value (up to 64 KB); clears the field and sets the value as typing would (input and change events). fill_secret: as fill, with secret, the name of an entry in the request's secrets; it is typed only into a field whose frame is at one of the secret's origins, over https (else the action fails with secret_origin_mismatch, or secret_insecure). press: key (Enter, Tab, Control+a...), selector optional. select: selector and value or label. scroll: to (top, bottom) or px. navigate: url (https; on allow_hosts when given), in the same tab. evaluate: script (up to 64 KB) run in the page's own world; mode expression (default) gives the completion value of the script, as a console does, and function runs it as a function body with args (JSON up to 64 KB) and gives what it returns. A promise is awaited; the value comes back as JSON (up to 1 MB) in data.actions[i].value. A script that sends the page elsewhere ends ok with value null, and the next action runs in the new document. wait_for_response: url_contains or url_regex, method, status_in (HTTP statuses) and body (text (default) or none); matches the first response, as the browser's network layer saw it, to a request that started after the previous action began (any, for the first action) and that completes, and returns it in data.actions[i].response. type: text typed one key at a time, selector optional, delay_ms (0 to 1000) between keys.

args.description: Any JSON value, only with mode function: the function's args.

ActionResponse.description: The response a wait_for_response matched, from the browser's network layer (not the page's JavaScript): the exact request URL with its query, and the real HTTP status.

request_index.description: Its index in the network capture, when the request has capture and recorded it.

headers.description: Lowercased names; Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization and secret-named headers masked as in a capture.

body.description: With body text: the body, utf-8 text for text types, else base64; up to 2 MB (8 MB for all of a request's action results). null with body none, or for a response without one.

complete.description: Whether the whole body was read.

truncated.description: Whether body holds less than the whole body.

sha256.description: Of the whole body. null when one of the request's secrets was taken out of it.

action_index_started.description: The action that set the request off: the one running when it started, or, when that was a wait, the action before it.

status.description: skipped: an earlier action that was not optional failed, or the page did not answer 2xx.

value.description: evaluate only: the script's result as JSON.

message.description: What went wrong, with the failing selector at most; for evaluate_error, the script's own error. page_not_ok: the page answered other than 2xx, so no action ran.

type.description: What the request was: a browser resource type (document, script, xhr, fetch...), connection (a socket, worker or redirect hop the relay refused) or redirect (an HTTP redirect).

action_index.description: The action that set it off, or null.

Login.description: A saved site login. The password is never returned; the username only masked.

site.description: The host FetchX may sign in on: the login is typed only on sign-in forms of this host and its subdomains, over https. A URL is taken as its host. It applies by itself to requests on the same registrable domain (login.example.com covers requests to app.example.com); name it with the request's `login` for a sign-in on another domain (an SSO provider).

status.description: new: not used yet. signed_in: FetchX signed in with it and keeps the session. rejected: the site showed its sign-in form again after the login was sent (a wrong password or unknown user), or several sign-ins in a row got no clear answer; code_required: the site asked for a one-time code. FetchX does not type a rejected or code_required login again until it is updated.

signed_in.description: Whether FetchX holds a signed-in session for it.

site.description: The host FetchX may sign in on: the login is typed only on sign-in forms of this host and its subdomains, over https. A URL is taken as its host. It applies by itself to requests on the same registrable domain (login.example.com covers requests to app.example.com); name it with the request's `login` for a sign-in on another domain (an SSO provider).

password.description: Stored sealed; never returned or logged, and taken out of stored pages and network captures.

id.description: The platform's id for the session (lowercase).

allow_hosts.description: The only hosts the session's browser may reach: exact hostnames, or *.suffix for every subdomain of suffix. Every request a page, frame or worker makes and every connection (WebSockets included) is held to it: one to a host off the list is refused before it leaves FetchX and listed in blocked_requests by origin. The first host decides the route's provider.

ttl_s.description: How long the session may run, from when it is open.

idle_ttl_s.description: The session closes when its caller sent nothing for this long (idle), or no caller was connected for this long (disconnect).

proxy.description: The exit: one IP for the whole session.

value.description: At most 4096 bytes. Never stored, logged or returned: held in the engine's memory while the request runs, and taken out of everything the request returns (as [REDACTED:<name>]) in the forms a page may send or show it (as typed, URL-encoded, form-encoded, JSON-escaped, base64). Shorter than 4 characters is refused: it could not be found to redact.

origins.description: The https origins (scheme, host, port; no path) the secret may be typed into or sent to. Each host must be in allow_hosts.

oneOf.description: The session's own secrets by name (1 to 8), each typed only at the origins it names (each origin's host must be on allow_hosts). Typed with POST .../fill, never sent to the caller: once loaded, a secret is taken out of everything the session sends its caller as [REDACTED:<name>] (in the forms a page may send or show it), and a request a page makes that carries it to another origin is stopped. The engine keeps their names and origins only.

login.description: A saved login (POST /internal/v1/logins) whose site is on allow_hosts: its signed-in session's cookies are in the browser from the start, and its username and password can be typed with fill (as login.username and login.password).

max_wire_bytes.description: Traffic (bytes on the wire, both ways, through the exit) at which the session closes (traffic_limit). At most the engine's setting (500 MB by default), which is also the default.

viewport.description: The pages' viewport; left out, the browser identity's own.

selector.description: A Playwright selector; the first match is filled.

frame_url.description: The start of the frame's https URL (for a field in a cross-origin frame); the main frame when left out.

BrowserSession.description: A remote browser session; once closed, its receipt.

ready_at.description: When its caller could first connect.

close_reason.description: client: closed with DELETE. ttl: reached ttl_s. idle: its caller sent nothing for idle_ttl_s. disconnect: no caller connected for idle_ttl_s. traffic_limit: reached max_wire_bytes. error: its browser failed or did not start (see error).

version.description: The Playwright release the session's server runs.

client.description: The major.minor a caller's Playwright must be (any patch release); another is refused with HTTP 428 at the WebSocket.

wire_bytes.description: Bytes through the exit, both ways, TLS included.

requests.description: Requests and connections the engine admitted.

connections.description: Caller connections over the session (null while it runs).

origin.description: Scheme, host and port (wss:// for a WebSocket).

type.description: A browser resource type (document, script, xhr, fetch...), websocket, or connection (a socket, worker request or redirect hop the relay refused).

blocked_requests.description: What was refused, by origin and type (each pair once, at most 100).

opened.description: WebSockets the pages opened to hosts on allow_hosts.

refused.description: WebSockets to hosts off the list (or not https), refused and listed in blocked_requests.

secret_egress.description: Secrets a page tried to send to another origin (the requests were stopped).

refused_calls.description: Protocol calls the session refused its caller, by Interface.method (such as Browser.newContext), with counts.

billable.description: null while it runs. true when it was open and ended in an ordinary way (any close_reason but error); the platform charges only those.

error.description: With close_reason error: a code, such as browser_failed, browser_deadline or engine_restarted.
